source_reviews.independent_solution: A nondegenerate segment AB has exactly two axes: its supporting line and its perpendicular bisector. An infinite line l has infinitely many axes: l itself and every line perpendicular to l. A reflection preserving a segment must preserve its two endpoints as a set. If it fixes both, its axis is the supporting line AB; if it swaps them, its axis is their perpendicular bisector. For an infinite line, reflection in that same line fixes every point, while reflection in any perpendicular line takes points to other points of l. A distinct parallel axis produces a displaced parallel line, and any oblique axis produces a differently directed line, so neither qualifies.

Constructing axes is also untested, although the original directly requests counts. source_reviews.independent_solution: The union of a nonzero-radius circumference and one full diameter segment has exactly two symmetry axes: the line containing the diameter and the perpendicular diameter line through the circle center. Both named reflections preserve the circumference and either fix or reverse the diameter segment. Conversely, the added diameter interior is the union's only straight interior segment, so a preserving reflection must preserve that segment and its endpoint pair. Its only possible axes are precisely its supporting line and perpendicular bisector. A circle alone has infinitely many axes, but its union with a specified diameter does not.
